facts.text: Fulton was founded in 1825 and became Callaway County’s seat, but it wasn’t incorporated until March 14, 1859.
The town was originally named Volney after the French historian, then renamed Fulton to honor inventor Robert Fulton two months later.
Winston Churchill delivered his famous “Iron Curtain” speech in Fulton on March 5, 1946, in front of President Harry S. Truman.
Downtown Fulton’s brick-lined streets form a historic district that still hosts modern shops, eateries, and art amid 19th‑century buildings.
The Callaway Nuclear Power Plant, Missouri’s only nuclear facility, sits just 13 miles southeast of Fulton and powers the state’s grid.
The National Churchill Museum, a landmark where Churchill spoke, sits across the street from Fulton’s historic downtown and attracts history buffs.
